newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON U.S. UNIT.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS FIRMER ON U.S. UNIT.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed firmer against the U.S. dollar on Monday after the central bank intervened to rescue the local unit from import pressure, dealers said.
"There was some import pressure in the morning and the Reserve Bank intervened with a sum of U.S.$5 million. A couple of banks were also selling and this pushed our dollar up," a dealer commented.

He said the local unit dipped to a low of 10.7650/7850 on increased demand for foreign currency but edged up after the central bank came into the market, to close at 10.7450/7650 against the U.S. dollar. This compared with 10.7550/7750 at the close of Friday trade.

It was also firmer against the mark at 6.9610/9775 from 7.0000/0200, tracking a stronger U.S. dollar on the German unit overseas, and gained a few points to 2.3170/3240 from 2.3300/3500 versus South Africa's rand.
Against pound sterling, however, the Zimbabwe dollar slipped to 18.0900/1350 from 18.0800/1000.
